description: This is a team in JR Tucker high school's astronomy club. I am Rishwitha and I am a club leader, who is interested in learning about astronomy.
summary: My team developed an interactive website that is fun for kids to explore and play around with. Because of the space "exploration" aspect of it, it is more enjoyable to students with short attention spans who can't pay attention to things like mission overviews and logs; there is more freedom and room for imagination to it. Kids need to be aware of the history behind all the science and technology we have today, and this starts with them having accessible learning tools.
details: Our website is an interactive, click-able solar system. The user can decide what planets they want to go to and what "abandoned" hardware they want to explore. It is sort of like a choose your own adventure except not a game; you get to decide where you want to go and learn about. This website gives school-age children an accessible site to learn about astronomy without getting bored or frustrated. With this project, our group intended to create a solar system simulation to aid curious kids. We used a variety of technological resources to create our project. We used Google Sites for the project itself, and within the project, we had a lot of different formats for all the hardware. Some of the hardware's information was in video format using Canva, some was in slideshow format using Google Slides, and some we put directly on the slide. We wanted to use many different tools to create it because we didn't want users to become bored of the same copy-paste format. The result was a conglomeration of ideas and formats meshed together; our project has the neat chaos of space itself. None of the people from the team had ever created a website before, so thinking of the idea was a creative feat in and of itself, but then the way we implemented the "choose your own" aspect was completely new and different.
